1.1.source: Databricks blog: What is a Data Lakehouse?
1.1.why: Classic architecture comparison: shows Data Warehouse (single purpose), Data Lake (multiple consumers but separate from warehouse), and Data Lakehouse (unified). Clearly illustrates the two-tier problem (left/middle panels) where organizations maintain separate systems with duplicate data.

1.1.source: Copy of Lakeflow Connect Tech Deck - L200, slide 20
1.1.why: BEFORE diagram: shows problem state of data fragmentation—SQL and Salesforce sources with manual extraction infrastructure, structured streaming, and custom notebooks needed to integrate them. Illustrates the operational complexity of data silos.

1.1.source: Copy of Lakeflow Connect Tech Deck - L200, slide 42
1.1.why: Query-based connectors: displays the breadth of data sources in the problem space (Applications, File sources, Databases, Warehouses, Message buses with vendor logos: SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Redshift). Visualizes the fragmentation companies maintain.

1.1.source: Copy of Lakeflow Connect Tech Deck - L200, slide 16
1.1.why: Lakeflow Connect roadmap organized by category (Applications, File sources, Databases, Warehouses, Message buses). Demonstrates the variety and complexity of siloed data systems companies manage separately.

1.2.why: Agent workflow showing the production blocker visually: step 3 'Deploy to pre-production' → step 4 'Fix quality issues' (red hexagon, blocking step) → step 5 'Deploy to production'. Shows the gap where pilots stall.

Agent Development Lifecycle showing progression: build prototype → test with humans → identify issues → fix code → test fixes → **get stakeholder sign-off** (highlighted box) → release. The feedback loop and gated production entry show why pilots stall.

Same lifecycle with operational tools highlighted on right (Tracing, Labeling, Evaluation datasets, Prompt Registry, LLM Judges, Evaluation UIs, Dashboards). Shows the operational complexity and tools required to reach production—the blocker.

Full Agent Framework & Evaluation - Production architecture: shows all production components (Vector Search, SQL Serverless, Model Serving, API Gateway, monitoring). Illustrates the operational infrastructure gap between prototype and production deployment.

Agent Framework & Evaluation - Production section showing governance and LLMOps controls (evaluation, monitoring). Emphasizes the control, governance, and quality gates required before production—why many pilots stop here.
